basis: Published portfolio cases and flow descriptions; not a new implementation audit.

projects.title: DQ Check Platform
projects.scope: Runs on session data in the browser. Associations are not proof of causation; this is not a deployed warehouse or production analytics service.

views.label: Logic flow
steps: Exclude invalid Actual and Expected rows and show how many were removed.
Calculate Actual - Expected ; when Expected is missing, use an explicitly labeled cohort-median fallback.
Group each remaining eligible dimension independently inside the current cohort.
Score drivers using grouped impact, distinctiveness, concentration, support, and a cardinality penalty.
Rank signed category contributions while preserving row counts and per-row movement.
Search supported two- and three-dimensional interaction segments after pruning weak candidates.
Repeat the full scan after every chart or chat drill.

views.label: Code flow
steps: Preserves identifiers, flattens shallow objects, enforces public-demo size limits, and records rejected rows.
Checks readiness, column behavior, missingness, duplicates, types, dates, outliers, variants, and PII-like fields.
Identifies reliable measures, comparison fields, eligible dimensions, labels, and valid hierarchy links.
Calculates residuals, rescans dimensions, ranks categories, and prunes supported interaction candidates.
Every click or deterministic-chat instruction changes the same cohort and repeats the scan.
Exports the quality report and treats news or analyst context as hypotheses rather than causal proof.

projects.title: Automated ML Pipeline Platform
projects.scope: Redrawn from the published pipeline case. This diagram is not a fresh audit of Azure resources, deployments, or model performance.

views.label: Logic flow
steps: Raw tabular data is validated, typed, and profiled before training begins.
The platform generates model and preprocessing combinations for the declared task family.
Candidates compete under repeatable cross-validation and optimization rules.
Metrics, parameters, artifacts, and lineage are recorded for every run.
The best candidate becomes a reusable, governed model output.

views.label: Code flow
steps: Reusable components orchestrate preparation, training, evaluation, and registration.
PyCaret, FLAML, and Optuna strategies generate candidate pipelines and hyperparameters.
Each run emits metrics, parameters, models, and artifacts into MLflow lineage.
Selection code ranks 457 recipes against the declared objective and constraints.
The winning model and metadata move into the governed model registry.

views.label: Data flow
steps: Input tables and feature candidates enter the Azure ML workspace.
Transforms produce train, validation, and test assets plus reusable preprocessing outputs.
Metrics, plots, models, and configuration snapshots accumulate in experiment storage.
The winning model, provenance, and evaluation metadata become a governed deployable asset.

projects.title: Governed AI Brain
projects.scope: The documented scaffold uses synthetic examples and an in-memory store. Production identity, durable storage, and stronger retrieval remain unfinished.

views.label: Logic flow
steps: A user, connector, or job submits source material with ownership, sensitivity, access, and version metadata.
Parsers, plugins, rules, or optional AI classify evidence and map it to the ontology.
A human approves, rejects, or requests changes while preserving warnings and provenance.
Approved objects become reusable brain records with explicit state and freshness.
The runtime selects allowed definitions, rules, caveats, relationships, and evidence for the task.
Applications, agents, notebooks, and pipelines receive the same governed context through the appropriate adapter.

views.label: Code flow
steps: API routes validate Pydantic contracts and delegate to shared services.
The compiler invokes enabled connectors, parsers, extractors, validators, and AI providers.
Review items and audit events are written without allowing direct publication.
Identity and access rules filter the candidate set before context is assembled.
A versioned context payload is returned with objects, evidence, caveats, freshness, and confidence.
REST, MCP, SDK, and CLI wrap the same core behavior instead of duplicating it.

views.label: Data flow
steps: Documents, SQL, dashboard exports, Markdown, and structured submissions arrive with source identity and policy data.
Original artifacts and normalized evidence chunks preserve what was actually provided.
Metrics, datasets, owners, rules, decisions, templates, and relationships remain explicitly unapproved.
Approved records carry state, lineage, source references, sensitivity, owner, reviewer, and freshness.
Only allowed and relevant knowledge reaches the application or model consuming the brain.

projects.title: Agentic Research Runtime
projects.scope: Logical runtime view from the case study, not a live infrastructure inventory. Claims require evidence and review before publication.

views.label: Logic flow
steps: The runtime receives a research request, required output, and quality constraints.
Agents decompose the task and gather source evidence through hybrid retrieval.
Claims, citations, source notes, and support relationships become inspectable graph objects.
Generation agents propose an answer while critique agents identify unsupported or incomplete parts.
The system loops until quality gates pass or an escalation condition is reached.
Only validated outputs are released together with traceable supporting evidence.

views.label: Code flow
steps: Durable orchestration manages agent execution, state, retries, and timeouts.
Lexical, semantic, and vector paths access indexed corpora and evidence stores.
DSPy-style modules plan, synthesize, cite, and format candidate outputs.
Promptfoo and test harnesses score grounding, completeness, formatting, and failure cases.
Failed outputs return to critique-and-repair; successful outputs move to publishing.

views.label: Data flow
steps: Documents, passages, and structured references become searchable evidence.
Embeddings and metadata support semantic retrieval and source linking.
Claims, citations, and support chains become first-class runtime records.
Scores, traces, failures, repaired drafts, and release decisions are retained for regression analysis.

projects.title: HarnessLab
projects.scope: One critic worker, one provider call, no tools, no child agents, and no external actions. Local versions are not cloud synchronization.

views.label: Logic flow
steps: The user supplies the goal, systems, constraints, success criteria, and known risks.
The planner decides whether deterministic software, an LLM feature, a workflow, a single agent, or bounded multi-agent guidance fits the requirement.
The result specifies topology, protocols, permissions, approvals, artifacts, failures, trace, and evaluation.
A compatible gateway may execute one temporary architecture critic against the validated plan.
Only typed medium/high-severity findings with confidence of at least 0.70 may add bounded review evidence.
The original and reviewed results remain available as immutable browser-local project versions and JSON exports.

views.label: Code flow
steps: GitHub Pages serves the command center and local project workspace without a build-time application server.
Browser mode runs the deterministic engine; automatic or required mode can call the configured gateway.
Every browser, fallback, gateway, and critic result must satisfy the same structured contract before rendering or saving.
The gateway validates the plan and builds a whitelist-only envelope that excludes credentials, tools, files, databases, and production data.
The fixed Architecture Critic uses the deterministic provider, configured Ollama model, or a free-only OpenRouter route.
Accepted findings may add questions and review evidence but cannot weaken permissions, stages, protocols, or constraints.

views.label: Data flow
steps: The full objective and constraints enter the project as the source input.
Architecture, permissions, planned agents, artifacts, trace, evaluation, and unresolved questions form one portable object.
Only approved result fields and the fixed worker policy cross the temporary-worker boundary.
Verdict, confidence, accepted findings, rejected findings, provider metadata, and failure evidence return as a typed artifact.
The reviewed result, original requirement, artifacts, and trace are retained locally and can be exported as JSON.

projects.title: ForkWise
projects.scope: Read-only review of commit-pinned evidence. Hosted runner jobs remain queued; this is decision support, not a security certification or legal opinion.

views.label: Logic flow
steps: The reviewer captures purpose, use case, deployment target, data sensitivity, team size, and external-service constraints.
Unsupported hosts and URL forms are rejected before evidence collection begins.
The review records the default branch and 40-character commit SHA so the result can be reproduced.
Metadata, the recursive tree, README, release information, and selected high-value text artifacts form the review snapshot.
Claims are marked verified, partial, unverified, contradicted, or not claimed based on inspected signals.
Fit, Trust, Run, Own, and Exit are evaluated against the user’s stated constraints.
The report recommends Adopt, Pilot, Fork, Avoid, or Insufficient evidence and records unresolved questions and a pilot checklist.

views.label: Code flow
steps: src/github.js normalizes the URL, translates API errors, pins the commit, and retrieves bounded repository evidence.
src/inventory.js classifies paths and selects the most useful text files within count and size limits.
src/analyzer.js generates deterministic evidence, findings, dimension summaries, claims, and recommendation logic.
src/schema.js enforces report enums, evidence references, unique identifiers, and credential-like text redaction.
src/app.js controls progress, filters, safe text rendering, and the GitHub-native reviewer experience.
src/export.js revalidates reports; runner clients and hosted adapters remain behind explicit activation and lifecycle gates.

views.label: Data flow
steps: Intent, use case, deployment target, sensitivity, team size, and external-service policy enter as normalized decision context.
Repository identity, branch, commit SHA, tree, README, release metadata, and selected text blobs form a bounded immutable reference.
Evidence records, finding references, severity, confidence, claim states, operational inventory, and unresolved questions remain linked.
The report records analyzer version, schema version, decision, confidence, five dimension summaries, and exact provenance.
Validated and re-redacted JSON or Markdown can be reviewed, compared, shared, or used to plan a controlled pilot.

projects.title: Mangrok Recipe Vault
projects.scope: Device-local use and optional cloud operations have different boundaries. Model work, print-provider handoff, and legacy release require their stated gates.

views.label: Logic flow
steps: A user adds recipe content, story, media, and a visibility class.
Sensitive notes are sealed before durable storage and separated from general metadata.
The owner grants scoped viewer, contributor, or custodian access with expiry and revocation.
Collaboration creates recoverable history so family knowledge can be restored.
Reviewed records become cookbook layouts and controlled print requests.
Inheritance requests enter a human-reviewed gate before private content is released.

views.label: Code flow
steps: The offline-capable client resolves local data and authenticated session state.
Web Crypto derives a key and encrypts secret fields before persistence.
Structured rows and private media references are submitted through authenticated APIs.
PostgreSQL row-level security decides which actor may read, edit, print, or administer.
A server-side function validates completeness and enforces idempotent provider handoff.

views.label: Data flow
steps: Recipe, ingredients, instructions, story, access class, and attachments enter the model.
General metadata, encrypted notes, and binary media are separated by sensitivity and storage needs.
PostgreSQL holds relational records while private object storage holds media behind signed access.
Sharing links, audit history, export bundles, and cookbook layouts derive from canonical records.

projects.title: Where It Happened
projects.scope: Design state stays in the browser. Checkout is a configured provider handoff or an explicit request fallback, never an invented payment success.

views.label: Architecture
steps: Map state and layout stay aligned

views.label: Logic flow
steps: The user selects a city, landmark, geolocation, or exact coordinates.
Map mood, story preset, layout, caption, and output format shape the poster.
The live creator keeps the map and poster state synchronized as controls change.
The design is stored locally, encoded into a URL hash, or exported as PNG/PDF.
A real provider handoff occurs only when checkout is configured; otherwise the app uses an explicit request fallback.

views.label: Code flow
steps: GitHub Pages serves the core UI before the heavier map runtime is requested.
MapLibre initializes the map with OpenFreeMap vector styles and active theme layers.
Control events update a central design object that drives rendering, local persistence, and sharing.
The poster view becomes a watermarked image or browser-printable PDF.
Code redirects to a configured provider or shows a transparent order-request path.

views.label: Data flow
steps: Preset data, search results, geolocation, or manual coordinates form the geographic anchor.
Color mood, labels, layout, crop, zoom, marker state, and text become a serializable object.
Drafts and cart snapshots live locally while shareable state is compressed into the URL hash.
A sanitized product and design payload reaches the checkout adapter or order-request fallback.

projects.title: My Seventh Meal
projects.scope: This is the proposed design, not a claim of a released nutrition service. AI proposes candidates; confirmed structure and references drive calculation.

views.label: Logic flow
steps: The user photographs a plate or enters the meal manually.
A multimodal model proposes one to three plausible dishes or components.
The system asks only clarifications likely to materially change the result.
The user confirms dishes, portions, oils, sides, ingredients, and recipe variations.
A versioned engine calculates nutrients from structured food records and reference data.
Corrections become reusable meal and household-recipe memory for future logging.

views.label: Code flow
steps: The React Native client uploads a photo or manual meal object to the API.
A provider-abstracted multimodal service returns candidates and uncertainty signals.
A clarification policy selects the smallest useful set of follow-up questions.
Confirmed structure maps to canonical foods and versioned deterministic calculation rules.
Corrected meal profiles and household recipes are saved for reuse.

views.label: Data flow
steps: Photo pixels and text descriptions arrive as evidence, not as final truth.
Confirmation converts evidence into dishes, ingredients, yields, oils, portions, and provenance.
Canonical food records resolve against curated and USDA-aligned nutrient sources.
The result stores nutrients, ranges, confidence notes, and the calculation version that produced them.
